summary: Richard Fick was an Indologist who studied at Kiel University (~1885–1888). He worked at Kiel University Library (1886–1897), the Royal Library of Berlin (1897), and served as head of the Göttingen State and University Library (1921–1932).

Richard Foltz works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and history. He studied at the University of Utah (~1982–1988) and Harvard (~1991–1996), later serving as Founding Director of the Centre for Iranian Studies at Concordia University (~2006–2026).
Richard Fritzsche was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1870–1875). He later served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg (~1888–1913).

Richard G. Salomon is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who studied under Ludo Rocher (~1970–1975). He was a professor at the University of Washington (~1981–2021) and a visiting researcher at Soka University (2007).

Richard Gombrich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Oxford and under Walpola Rahula and K. R. Norman. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1965–2004) and President of the Pali Text Society (1994–2002).

Richard Hartshorne studied at Princeton University (~1916–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1920–1924). He held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).

Richard Hauschild was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Jena, and Tübingen under Johannes Hertel and Albert Debrunner. He spent his career at the University of Jena, serving as Lektor (1938) and professor (1951–1967).

Richard Henebry was a linguist who studied at St. John's College, St Patrick's Pontifical University, and the universities of Greifswald and Freiburg. He also studied under Heinrich Zimmer (~1896–1898).

Richard Hugh Robinson was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Alberta, SOAS, and the University of London under Edward Conze, David Snellgrove, Arthur Waley, and David Friedman, later becoming a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1961).

Richard Hughes Seager is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1982–1987), and was an Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994).

Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University (~1968–1972) and Harvard University (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as a psychology professor from 2001 to 2017.

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (by 1988), studying under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa and traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean of the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1994–2017) and on the faculty of the Graduate Theological Union (~1995).
Richard Keith Sprigg was a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology who studied at Oakham School. He held an academic post at SOAS University of London and the University of London (~1948–1980).

Richard Kieckhefer is a historian of religion who studied at Saint Louis University and the University of Texas at Austin. He became a professor of history and religious studies at Northwestern University in 1975 and served as President of Societas Magica (1995–2004).

Richard King is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied under Daniel Mariau and at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster. He held posts at the University of Stirling (~1993–2003), Vanderbilt (~2003–2011), and the University of Glasgow (~2010–2012).
Richard M. Eaton is a scholar of history and Indology. He studied at the College of Wooster (~1958–1962) and served as Professor of History at the University of Arizona (~1972).

Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1992–1999) and Duke University, where he became Professor of Religious Studies (~1999).

Richard Morris was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at Battersea Training College. He served as headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888) and was Ex-President of the Philological Society (~1871–1874).

Richard P. Boyle completed graduate work at the University of Washington and studied under Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held a post at the University of New Mexico (attested 2015).
